subject: math
title: Coordinates, Translations and Reflections on a Grid
seo_title: Grade 4 Coordinates Worksheets: Plot Points, Translations and Reflections (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Plot and read coordinates in the first quadrant of a Cartesian plane, and describe the translations that move a point from one coordinate to another
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on coordinates for the Ontario curriculum: read and plot points in the first quadrant, describe translations, reflect points and shapes in a mirror line, and solve map and coding problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: In (x, y), go across x first, then up y.
key_sub: (2, 6) and (6, 2) are different points. A translation slides: right and left change x, up and down change y. A reflection flips a point over a mirror line to the same distance on the other side.
body_html:
Reading and plotting points

A coordinate grid has two number lines. The x-axis goes across. The y-axis goes up. They meet at the origin, (0, 0).

An ordered pair (x, y) tells you how to reach a point from the origin. Go across first, then up. The first number is how far across. The second number is how far up.

Example

A point is 6 units across from the origin and 2 units up. What are its coordinates?

Across 6 is the x-coordinate. Up 2 is the y-coordinate. Write the across number first.

Answer: (6, 2)

Order matters. (4, 5) and (5, 4) are different points. A point on the x-axis has y = 0, such as (3, 0). A point on the y-axis has x = 0, such as (0, 3).

Translations: slide

A translation slides a point or shape without turning or flipping it. One square on the grid is 1 unit. Moving right or left changes only x. Moving up or down changes only y.

MoveWhat changesExample from (5, 4)
2 rightx gets bigger(7, 4)
2 leftx gets smaller(3, 4)
2 upy gets bigger(5, 6)
2 downy gets smaller(5, 2)
Example

Describe the translation from (1, 6) to (4, 2).

Across: 1 to 4 is 3 units right. Up and down: 6 to 2 is 4 units down.

Answer: 3 units right and 4 units down

Reflections: flip

A reflection flips a point or shape over a mirror line. The reflection is the same distance from the line, on the other side.

A vertical mirror line (straight up and down) changes only x. A horizontal mirror line (straight across) changes only y.

Example

Reflect (5, 1) in the horizontal mirror line through 3 on the y-axis.

(5, 1) is 2 units below the line. The reflection is 2 units above it: 3 + 2 = 5. x stays 5.

Answer: (5, 5)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Swapping x and y: plotting (3, 7) at across 7, up 3Go across first (x), then up (y)
Counting the start line as 1The origin is 0. Count the jumps between lines
Counting the start square as a moveStart counting with your first jump
Moving the wrong way: adding for “left”Left and down make the number smaller
Stopping on the mirror lineGo the same distance past the line
Changing y for a vertical mirror lineA vertical line changes x; a horizontal line changes y

faq.q: What do Grade 4 students learn about coordinates in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: In Grade 4 (Spatial Sense, E1.2 and E1.3), students plot and read points in the first quadrant, describe the translation that moves one point to another, and perform translations and reflections on a grid.

faq.q: Which comes first in an ordered pair, x or y?
faq.a: The x-coordinate always comes first. (3, 7) means go across 3, then up 7. A simple tip is “across first, then up.”

faq.q: How do you reflect a point on a grid?
faq.a: Count how many units the point is from the mirror line, then count the same number of units on the other side. A vertical mirror line changes only x, and a horizontal mirror line changes only y.

faq.q: What is the difference between a translation and a reflection?
faq.a: A translation slides a shape left, right, up or down, so it still faces the same way. A reflection flips the shape over a mirror line, so it faces the opposite way, like your image in a mirror.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 4, then up 6. Point A is at (4, 6). Go across first (x), then up (y).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 5, then up 3. Point B is at (5, 3). Go across first (x), then up (y).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point C?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 2, then up 6. Point C is at (2, 6). Go across first (x), then up (y). (6, 2) is point D: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point E?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 7, then up 4. Point E is at (7, 4). Go across first (x), then up (y). (4, 7) is point F: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point G?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 1, then up 3. Point G is at (1, 3). Go across first (x), then up (y). (3, 1) is point H: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point J?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 8, then up 5. Point J is at (8, 5). Go across first (x), then up (y).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point K?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 6, then up 9. Point K is at (6, 9). Go across first (x), then up (y). (9, 6) is point L: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point M?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 3, then up 2. Point M is at (3, 2). Go across first (x), then up (y).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point N?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 9, then up 8. Point N is at (9, 8). Go across first (x), then up (y).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point Q?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 7, then up 7. Point Q is at (7, 7). Go across first (x), then up (y).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point S?
items.e: Point S is on the y-axis, so it does not go across at all: x = 0. It goes up 5. S is at (0, 5).

items.q: What are the coordinates of point V?
items.e: Point V is on the x-axis. Go across 7 and up 0: (7, 0). A point on the x-axis always has y = 0.

items.q: What is the x-coordinate of point W?
items.e: The x-coordinate tells you how far across to go. Point W is 6 units across from the origin, so x = 6. (3 is its y-coordinate.)

items.q: What is the y-coordinate of point U?
items.e: The y-coordinate tells you how far up to go. Point U is 5 units up, so y = 5. (2 is its x-coordinate.)

items.q: What is the x-coordinate of point Z?
items.e: Point Z is 8 units across from the origin, so its x-coordinate is 8. Point Y is the one at (4, 8).

items.q: In the ordered pair (5, 8), which number comes first?
items.e: An ordered pair is always written (x, y). The number for across comes first, then the number for up.

items.q: Which tip helps you plot a point such as (3, 6)?
c: Start at the top of the grid
items.e: Think of walking to an elevator before you ride it up. Go across the x-axis first, then up: (x, y).

items.q: In the ordered pair (7, 3), what does the 3 tell you?
items.e: The second number is the y-coordinate. It tells you how far to go up: up 3. The 7 tells you to go across 7 first.

items.q: What are the coordinates of the origin, where the x-axis and the y-axis meet?
items.e: The origin is 0 on both axes. You have not moved across or up, so it is (0, 0).

items.q: Mei starts at (0, 0). She goes across 3, then up 8. What are the coordinates of her point?
items.e: Across 3 gives x = 3 and up 8 gives y = 8. Write the across number first: (3, 8).

items.q: Which point is at (5, 2)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 5, then up 2: that is point A. Point B is at (2, 5): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (2, 7)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 2, then up 7: that is point B. Point A is at (7, 2): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (1, 4)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 1, then up 4: that is point C. Point A is at (4, 1): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (7, 3)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 7, then up 3: that is point D. Point A is at (3, 7): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (3, 8)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 3, then up 8: that is point C. Point A is at (8, 3): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (6, 4)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 6, then up 4: that is point A. Point B is at (4, 6): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (2, 5)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 2, then up 5: that is point B. Point A is at (5, 2): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (4, 1)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 4, then up 1: that is point D. Point A is at (1, 4): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (8, 6)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 8, then up 6: that is point C. Point A is at (6, 8): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point is at (3, 9)?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 3, then up 9: that is point B. Point A is at (9, 3): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: Which point has an x-coordinate of 6?
items.e: The x-coordinate is the first number: how far across. Point A is 6 units across, at (6, 2). The point at (2, 6) has a y-coordinate of 6, not an x-coordinate of 6.

items.q: Which point has a y-coordinate of 4?
items.e: The y-coordinate is the second number: how far up. Point D is 4 units up, at (5, 4). The point at (4, 5) has an x-coordinate of 4.

items.q: Leah says point B is at (5, 2). What mistake did she make?
c: She counted the start line as 1
items.e: Point B is 2 units across and 5 units up, so it is at (2, 5). Leah wrote the up number first.

items.q: Aiden says point E is at (4, 5). What mistake did he make?
c: He counted the start line as 1
items.e: Point E is at (3, 4). Aiden counted the line at 0 as 1, so both numbers came out 1 too big. The origin is 0: count the jumps.

items.q: Are (3, 6) and (6, 3) the same point?
c: Yes, they use the same numbers
Yes, the order does not matter
items.e: (3, 6) is across 3, up 6. (6, 3) is across 6, up 3. The order of the numbers changes where the point is.

items.q: Benjamin wants to plot (8, 2). He goes up 8, then across 2. Which point did he plot by mistake?
items.e: Going across 2 and up 8 lands on (2, 8). To plot (8, 2), go across 8 first, then up 2.

items.q: Which point is farther to the right: (3, 9) or (7, 2)?
items.e: How far right a point is depends on the x-coordinate, the first number. 7 is more than 3, so (7, 2) is farther right.

items.q: Which point is higher on the grid: (9, 2) or (1, 6)?
items.e: How high a point is depends on the y-coordinate, the second number. 6 is more than 2, so (1, 6) is higher.

items.q: Which point is straight above (5, 1)?
items.e: Points straight above each other have the same x-coordinate. (5, 7) has x = 5, the same as (5, 1), and a bigger y.

items.q: Which point is straight to the right of (2, 4)?
items.e: Points straight across from each other have the same y-coordinate. (8, 4) has y = 4, the same as (2, 4), and a bigger x.

items.q: Point A is at (2, 4). It is translated 3 units right and 2 units up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Right 3 units changes x: 2 + 3 = 5. Up 2 changes y: 4 + 2 = 6. The new point is (5, 6).

items.q: Point A is at (3, 2). It is translated 6 units up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: x stays 3. Up 6 changes y: 2 + 6 = 8. The new point is (3, 8).

items.q: Point A is at (8, 5). It is translated 5 units left. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 5 units changes x: 8 − 5 = 3. y stays 5. The new point is (3, 5).

items.q: Point A is at (1, 7). It is translated 4 units right and 3 units down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Right 4 units changes x: 1 + 4 = 5. Down 3 changes y: 7 − 3 = 4. The new point is (5, 4).

items.q: Point A is at (7, 2). It is translated 2 units left and 5 units up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 2 units changes x: 7 − 2 = 5. Up 5 changes y: 2 + 5 = 7. The new point is (5, 7).

items.q: Point A is at (9, 9). It is translated 4 units left and 6 units down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 4 units changes x: 9 − 4 = 5. Down 6 changes y: 9 − 6 = 3. The new point is (5, 3).

items.q: Point P is translated 3 units right and 2 units up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Right 3 units changes x: 5 + 3 = 8. Up 2 changes y: 1 + 2 = 3. The new point is (8, 3). That is point C.

items.q: Point P is translated 4 units right and 3 units down. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Right 4 units changes x: 2 + 4 = 6. Down 3 changes y: 7 − 3 = 4. The new point is (6, 4). That is point B.

items.q: Point P is translated 3 units left and 4 units up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Left 3 units changes x: 7 − 3 = 4. Up 4 changes y: 2 + 4 = 6. The new point is (4, 6). That is point D.

items.q: Point P is translated 5 units left and 2 units down. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Left 5 units changes x: 8 − 5 = 3. Down 2 changes y: 8 − 2 = 6. The new point is (3, 6). That is point A.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (1, 2) and B is at (4, 4). Across: 1 to 4 is 3 units right. Up and down: 2 to 4 is 2 units up. Count the jumps, not the start.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (6, 3) and B is at (2, 3). Across: 6 to 2 is 4 units left. The y-coordinate stays 3, so there is no move up or down. Count the jumps, not the start.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (2, 6) and B is at (5, 1). Across: 2 to 5 is 3 units right. Up and down: 6 to 1 is 5 units down. Count the jumps, not the start.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (7, 6) and B is at (3, 2). Across: 7 to 3 is 4 units left. Up and down: 6 to 2 is 4 units down. Count the jumps, not the start.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (4, 1) and B is at (4, 6). The x-coordinate stays 4, so there is no move left or right. Up and down: 1 to 6 is 5 units up. Count the jumps, not the start.

items.q: A point moves from (3, 8) to (9, 4). Describe the translation.
items.e: The start is at (3, 8) and the end is at (9, 4). Across: 3 to 9 is 6 units right. Up and down: 8 to 4 is 4 units down. Count the jumps, not the start.

items.q: A point moves from (8, 2) to (1, 7). Describe the translation.
items.e: The start is at (8, 2) and the end is at (1, 7). Across: 8 to 1 is 7 units left. Up and down: 2 to 7 is 5 units up. Count the jumps, not the start.

items.q: Point B is translated 3 units right and 2 units up. It lands on (8, 6). Where did it start?
items.e: Work backwards: undo each move. 3 right is undone by 3 left: 8 − 3 = 5. 2 up is undone by 2 down: 6 − 2 = 4. B started at (5, 4).

items.q: Owen translates (6, 5) 4 units left and gets (10, 5). What mistake did he make?
items.e: Moving left makes the x-coordinate smaller: 6 − 4 = 2. The correct answer is (2, 5). Owen added 4, which is a move to the right.

items.q: A point is translated left or right. Which coordinate changes?
items.e: Left and right is the x direction. The point does not move up or down, so the y-coordinate stays the same.

items.q: The blue dashed line is a mirror line. Point P is reflected in it. What are the coordinates of the reflection?
items.e: P is at (2, 3). The mirror line goes straight up through 4. P is 2 units left of the line, so the reflection is 2 units right of the line: 4 + 2 = 6. A vertical mirror line changes only x; y stays 3. The reflection is (6, 3).

items.q: The blue dashed line is a mirror line. Point P is reflected in it. What are the coordinates of the reflection?
items.e: P is at (7, 2). The mirror line goes straight up through 5. P is 2 units right of the line, so the reflection is 2 units left of the line: 5 − 2 = 3. A vertical mirror line changes only x; y stays 2. The reflection is (3, 2).

items.q: The blue dashed line is a mirror line. Point P is reflected in it. What are the coordinates of the reflection?
items.e: P is at (3, 1). The mirror line goes straight across through 3. P is 2 units below the line, so the reflection is 2 units above the line: 3 + 2 = 5. A horizontal mirror line changes only y; x stays 3. The reflection is (3, 5).

items.q: The blue dashed line is a mirror line. Point P is reflected in it. What are the coordinates of the reflection?
items.e: P is at (5, 6). The mirror line goes straight across through 4. P is 2 units above the line, so the reflection is 2 units below the line: 4 − 2 = 2. A horizontal mirror line changes only y; x stays 5. The reflection is (5, 2).

items.q: The blue dashed line is a mirror line. Point P is reflected in it. What are the coordinates of the reflection?
items.e: P is at (1, 5). The mirror line goes straight up through 4. P is 3 units left of the line, so the reflection is 3 units right of the line: 4 + 3 = 7. A vertical mirror line changes only x; y stays 5. The reflection is (7, 5).

items.q: The blue dashed line is a mirror line. Point P is reflected in it. What are the coordinates of the reflection?
items.e: P is at (4, 7). The mirror line goes straight across through 5. P is 2 units above the line, so the reflection is 2 units below the line: 5 − 2 = 3. A horizontal mirror line changes only y; x stays 4. The reflection is (4, 3).

items.q: Point P is reflected in the blue dashed mirror line. Which point shows the reflection?
items.e: P is at (3, 4). The mirror line goes straight up through 5. P is 2 units left of the line, so the reflection is 2 units right of the line: 5 + 2 = 7. A vertical mirror line changes only x; y stays 4. The reflection is (7, 4). That is point C. Point A is on the mirror line: the reflection goes past the line, not onto it.

items.q: Point P is reflected in the blue dashed mirror line. Which point shows the reflection?
items.e: P is at (6, 2). The mirror line goes straight across through 4. P is 2 units below the line, so the reflection is 2 units above the line: 4 + 2 = 6. A horizontal mirror line changes only y; x stays 6. The reflection is (6, 6). That is point A. Point B is on the mirror line: the reflection goes past the line, not onto it.

items.q: Point P is reflected in the blue dashed mirror line. Which point shows the reflection?
items.e: P is at (8, 5). The mirror line goes straight up through 6. P is 2 units right of the line, so the reflection is 2 units left of the line: 6 − 2 = 4. A vertical mirror line changes only x; y stays 5. The reflection is (4, 5). That is point B. Point A is on the mirror line: the reflection goes past the line, not onto it.

items.q: Point P is reflected in the blue dashed mirror line. Which point shows the reflection?
items.e: P is at (1, 7). The mirror line goes straight across through 5. P is 2 units above the line, so the reflection is 2 units below the line: 5 − 2 = 3. A horizontal mirror line changes only y; x stays 1. The reflection is (1, 3). That is point D. Point A is on the mirror line: the reflection goes past the line, not onto it.

items.q: The rectangle has corners at (1, 2), (3, 2), (3, 5) and (1, 5). It is reflected in the blue dashed mirror line. Where does the red corner at (3, 5) go?
items.e: The red corner is at (3, 5). The mirror line goes straight up through 5. The red corner is 2 units left of the line, so the reflection is 2 units right of the line: 5 + 2 = 7. A vertical mirror line changes only x; y stays 5. The reflection is (7, 5). (9, 5) is where the corner at (1, 5) goes, so it belongs to a different corner.

items.q: The rectangle has corners at (2, 1), (6, 1), (6, 3) and (2, 3). It is reflected in the blue dashed mirror line. Where does the red corner at (6, 3) go?
items.e: The red corner is at (6, 3). The mirror line goes straight across through 4. The red corner is 1 unit below the line, so the reflection is 1 unit above the line: 4 + 1 = 5. A horizontal mirror line changes only y; x stays 6. The reflection is (6, 5). (6, 7) is where the corner at (6, 1) goes, so it belongs to a different corner.

items.q: The rectangle has corners at (6, 6), (8, 6), (8, 8) and (6, 8). It is reflected in the blue dashed mirror line. Where does the red corner at (6, 8) go?
items.e: The red corner is at (6, 8). The mirror line goes straight up through 5. The red corner is 1 unit right of the line, so the reflection is 1 unit left of the line: 5 − 1 = 4. A vertical mirror line changes only x; y stays 8. The reflection is (4, 8). (2, 8) is where the corner at (8, 8) goes, so it belongs to a different corner.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Which move is it?
c: a reflection in a vertical line
a reflection in a horizontal line
items.e: Shape B points the same way as shape A. It has only slid 5 units right and 3 units up, so it is a translation.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Which move is it?
c: a reflection in a vertical line
a reflection in a horizontal line
items.e: Shape B is flipped left to right: its foot points the other way. The two shapes are the same distance from a vertical line through 5, so it is a reflection in a vertical line.

items.q: Shape A is moved to shape B. Which move is it?
c: a reflection in a vertical line
a reflection in a horizontal line
items.e: Shape B is flipped upside down: its foot is now at the top. The shapes are the same distance from a horizontal line through 5, so it is a reflection in a horizontal line.

items.q: A point is reflected in a vertical mirror line. Which coordinate changes?
items.e: A vertical mirror line flips the point across, to the left or right. The point does not go up or down, so y stays the same.

items.q: Point P is 3 units to the left of a vertical mirror line. Where is its reflection?
c: 3 units to the right of the line
3 units to the left of the line
6 units to the right of the line
items.e: A reflection is the same distance from the mirror line, on the other side. 3 units left becomes 3 units right.

items.q: Priya reflects (2, 5) in the vertical mirror line through 4 on the x-axis and gets (4, 5). What mistake did she make?
c: She stopped on the mirror line
items.e: (2, 5) is 2 units left of the line through 4. The reflection is 2 units right of the line: 4 + 2 = 6. The answer is (6, 5). Priya only moved to the line.

items.q: A point is right on the mirror line. Where is its reflection?
items.e: The point is 0 units from the mirror line, so its reflection is also 0 units away: it does not move.

items.q: The map shows a town. S = school, R = skating rink, L = library, F = fire station, G = grocery store. Each unit is 1 block. What are the coordinates of the skating rink?
items.e: Start at (0, 0). Go across 6, then up 7. The rink is at (6, 7). (7, 6) has the numbers swapped.

items.q: The map shows a town. S = school, R = skating rink, L = library, F = fire station, G = grocery store. Each unit is 1 block. What is at (8, 3)?
items.e: Go across 8, then up 3: that is L, the library.

items.q: The map shows a town. S = school, R = skating rink, L = library, F = fire station, G = grocery store. Each unit is 1 block. Hana leaves the school. She walks 4 blocks right and 2 blocks up. Where is she now?
items.e: The school is at (1, 2). Right 4: 1 + 4 = 5. Up 2: 2 + 2 = 4. (5, 4) is the grocery store.

items.q: The map shows a town. S = school, R = skating rink, L = library, F = fire station, G = grocery store. Each unit is 1 block. Describe the move from the library to the skating rink.
items.e: The library is at (8, 3) and the rink is at (6, 7). Across: 8 to 6 is 2 units left. Up and down: 3 to 7 is 4 units up. Count the jumps, not the start.

items.q: The map shows a town. S = school, R = skating rink, L = library, F = fire station, G = grocery store. Each unit is 1 block. A fire truck drives along the streets (the grid lines) from the fire station to the library. What is the shortest number of blocks?
items.e: The fire station is at (2, 6) and the library is at (8, 3). Go 8 − 2 = 6 blocks right and 6 − 3 = 3 blocks down. 6 + 3 = 9 blocks.

items.q: The map shows a town. S = school, R = skating rink, L = library, F = fire station, G = grocery store. Each unit is 1 block. A new park is built 3 blocks left of the library. What are its coordinates?
items.e: The library is at (8, 3). Left 3 changes only x: 8 − 3 = 5. y stays 3: (5, 3).

items.q: The map shows a lake at the cottage. D = dock, C = cottage, I = island, N = loon nest, B = beach. Each unit is 100 m. What are the coordinates of the island?
items.e: Go across 5, then up 4. The island is at (5, 4).

items.q: The map shows a lake at the cottage. D = dock, C = cottage, I = island, N = loon nest, B = beach. Each unit is 100 m. Chloe paddles a canoe from the dock 4 units right and 3 units up. Where does she land?
items.e: The dock is at (1, 1). Right 4: 1 + 4 = 5. Up 3: 1 + 3 = 4. (5, 4) is the island.

items.q: The map shows a lake at the cottage. D = dock, C = cottage, I = island, N = loon nest, B = beach. Each unit is 100 m. Describe the move from the island to the loon nest.
items.e: The island is at (5, 4) and the loon nest is at (6, 6). Across: 5 to 6 is 1 unit right. Up and down: 4 to 6 is 2 units up. Count the jumps, not the start.

items.q: The map shows a lake at the cottage. D = dock, C = cottage, I = island, N = loon nest, B = beach. Each unit is 100 m. How many units is it from the dock straight up to the cottage?
items.e: The dock is at (1, 1) and the cottage is at (1, 4). The x-coordinate stays 1, so subtract the y-coordinates: 4 − 1 = 3 units.

items.q: The map shows a lake at the cottage. D = dock, C = cottage, I = island, N = loon nest, B = beach. Each unit is 100 m. Emma paddles from the island 2 units left and 3 units down. What are the coordinates of the spot where she stops?
items.e: The island is at (5, 4). Left 2: 5 − 2 = 3. Down 3: 4 − 3 = 1. Emma stops at (3, 1).

items.q: The seating plan shows where some students sit. L = Liam, M = Maya, A = Arjun, Z = Zoe, T = teacher’s desk. What are the coordinates of Zoe’s desk?
items.e: Go across 5, then up 3. Zoe sits at (5, 3). (3, 5) has the numbers swapped.

items.q: The seating plan shows where some students sit. L = Liam, M = Maya, A = Arjun, Z = Zoe, T = teacher’s desk. Who sits at (1, 4)?
items.e: Go across 1, then up 4: that is A, Arjun. Maya is at (4, 1), with the numbers the other way round.

items.q: The seating plan shows where some students sit. L = Liam, M = Maya, A = Arjun, Z = Zoe, T = teacher’s desk. Describe the move from Liam’s desk to Zoe’s desk.
items.e: Liam is at (1, 1) and Zoe is at (5, 3). Across: 1 to 5 is 4 units right. Up and down: 1 to 3 is 2 units up. Count the jumps, not the start.

items.q: In a coding lesson, Liam’s robot starts at (2, 1). The code says: move 3 right, move 4 up, move 1 left. Where does the robot stop?
items.e: Follow one move at a time. 3 right: (5, 1). 4 up: (5, 5). 1 left: (4, 5). Left makes x smaller.

items.q: A robot is at (1, 2). Which line of code moves it to (6, 2)?
items.e: The y-coordinate stays 2, so the robot only moves across. 6 − 1 = 5, and x gets bigger, so it moves 5 right. Count the jumps, not the start.

items.q: Zoe is making a symmetrical design on grid paper for art class. The mirror line is the vertical line through 5 on the x-axis. She draws a dot at (3, 6). Where should the matching dot go?
items.e: The dot is at (3, 6). The mirror line goes straight up through 5. The dot is 2 units left of the line, so the reflection is 2 units right of the line: 5 + 2 = 7. A vertical mirror line changes only x; y stays 6. The reflection is (7, 6).

items.q: Mateo draws half of a butterfly. The body is a vertical mirror line through 6 on the x-axis. The tip of the left wing is at (2, 7). Where is the tip of the right wing?
items.e: The left wing tip is at (2, 7). The mirror line goes straight up through 6. The left wing tip is 4 units left of the line, so the reflection is 4 units right of the line: 6 + 4 = 10. A vertical mirror line changes only x; y stays 7. The reflection is (10, 7).

items.q: Ava folds grid paper along the horizontal line through 4 on the y-axis. A paint dot at (5, 1) is printed on the other side of the fold. Where is the new dot?
items.e: The paint dot is at (5, 1). The mirror line goes straight across through 4. The paint dot is 3 units below the line, so the reflection is 3 units above the line: 4 + 3 = 7. A horizontal mirror line changes only y; x stays 5. The reflection is (5, 7). Folding paper makes a reflection.

items.q: On a plan of the schoolyard, a soccer net is a rectangle with corners at (1, 5), (3, 5), (3, 6) and (1, 6). The net is moved 4 units right and 2 units down. What are the new coordinates of the corner at (3, 6)?
items.e: Right 4 units changes x: 3 + 4 = 7. Down 2 changes y: 6 − 2 = 4. The new point is (7, 4). Every corner moves the same way, so the net stays the same size.
